name: Kenji Kasahara
current_role: Founder, Director and Senior Corporate Officer, MIXI, Inc. (Tokyo)
profile: Kasahara founded Japanese social network Mixi in 2004 and took it public in 2006. After Mixi lost ground to rivals he stepped back from CEO (2013) and the company pivoted to mobile games (Monster Strike), sports and lifestyle apps. He holds roughly half of MIXI and remains a director; in 2026 he announced a gift of ~1.8bn yen of his shares to ~1,700 employees.
interesting_fact: In May 2026 he announced he would personally donate about 680,000 MIXI shares (~1.8 billion yen) to around 1,700 group employees and officers, calling it a tangible way to express gratitude.
deep_cut_fact: Before Mixi, he built the job-listings site Find Job! in 1997 at age 21 while a University of Tokyo student, founding eMercury two years later; in 2015 he launched FamilyAlbum (Mitene), a private family photo-sharing app.
notes: Low public profile; best route is MIXI corporate press inquiry form. CEO is Hiroki Kimura.

name: Fan Meihua
current_role: Co-shareholder (with husband Yang Jianxin) in KJT / Global Top E-Commerce (跨境通, SZSE: 002640); no confirmed executive role
profile: Fan Meihua (樊梅花) is the wife and concert party of Yang Jianxin, founder of Shanxi-based Baiyuan Trousers, which became cross-border e-commerce group KJT (跨境通) after acquiring export e-retailers Globalegrow (环球易购) and Patozon. The couple were controlling holders; from 2019 they ceded voting control to a Guangzhou state-backed fund (unwound 2021) and sold down stakes. Little else is public.
interesting_fact: SZSE filings describe Yang Jianxin and Fan Meihua as legal spouses and formal 'persons acting in concert' who jointly controlled KJT until a 2019 voting-rights delegation to a Guangzhou Development District fund.
notes: Very private; no public profile found. Hurun listing (2016-2020) was via the couple's KJT stake, which has since shrunk sharply, so she is likely no longer a billionaire. Only route would be KJT board secretary (Wang Yuedi per 2025-26 IR records) via cninfo filings / ir.p5w.net.

name: Gina Vecchiarelli
current_role: Co-heir and principal shareholder (with sister Terry Leprino) of Leprino Foods, Denver; no public executive role
profile: Daughter of James Leprino, who built his father's 1950 Denver cheese shop into the world's largest mozzarella maker (supplier to Domino's, Pizza Hut, Papa John's). After his death in June 2025, she and her sister inherited a ~90% stake in the private company. She keeps a very low profile; her father said in 2016 she ran a program for Make-A-Wish.
interesting_fact: Leprino Foods makes more than 1 billion pounds of cheese a year; her father pioneered the technology to manufacture pizza mozzarella at industrial scale.

public_contacts.value: No email published; Leprino Corporate Communications media line 720-295-4815 (company press line)

notes: Very private, no public footprint found. Forbes says her husband Dan Vecchiarelli became chairman/CEO c.2023, but Leprino's own site names Lance FitzSimmons President & CEO (Oct 2024) and does not mention Vecchiarelli - verify before outreach. Only route is via Leprino corporate communications.

name: Jet Jie Li
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, J&T Global Express (HKEX: 1519)
profile: Li spent 15+ years at OPPO, leading its expansion into Indonesia and other Asian markets, then founded J&T Express in Jakarta in 2015. J&T became Southeast Asia's parcel-volume leader, entered China in 2020 (riding Pinduoduo's growth) and listed in Hong Kong in 2023; it now also operates in Saudi Arabia, UAE, Mexico, Brazil and Egypt.
interesting_fact: The 'J&T' name and brand were born in Indonesia, not China: Li launched it in Jakarta in June 2015 and only later took it back to China, now the group's largest market.
deep_cut_fact: OPPO's headquarters created the 'Jet Lee' award, named in his honour, to reward top salespeople across its global sales agencies. He holds a 1998 marketing degree from the University of Science and Technology Beijing and began at OPPO selling audiovisual products in 1999.
notes: Goes by 'Jet Lee' (李杰) in Indonesia. Rarely gives interviews; route via J&T IR/corporate communications.

name: Wee Wei Chi
current_role: Board member, Kheng Leong Co. (Wee family property and investment company), Singapore
profile: Younger daughter of the late Wee Cho Yaw (d. Feb 2024), longtime chairman of United Overseas Bank; her wealth stems from the family's UOB and related holdings. She sits on the board of Kheng Leong, the family's commercial property development and investment arm, and is married to David Eu of the Eu Yan Sang TCM family. Brother Wee Ee Cheong is UOB CEO.
interesting_fact: She studied fine arts, earning a bachelor's degree from Moravian University in Pennsylvania, an unusual path in a banking dynasty.
notes: Very private; no public contact or social accounts found. Forbes lists her as a former (dropped-off) billionaire. Any approach would likely need to go through the Wee family office / Kheng Leong, which publishes no contact for her.

name: Robert Douglas Haas
current_role: Chairman emeritus, Levi Strauss & Co.; trustee, Evelyn and Walter Haas, Jr. Fund
profile: Bob Haas (b. 1942), great-great-grandnephew of Levi Strauss, was Levi Strauss & Co.'s CEO (1984-1999) and chairman (1989-2008), leading its 1985 leveraged buyout back to private ownership and the growth of Dockers. He left the board in 2014 and now focuses on philanthropy via the family's Haas Jr. Fund and UC Berkeley programs.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Levi Strauss in 1992 became the first Fortune 500 company to extend health benefits to employees' unmarried partners, and was an early corporate responder to HIV/AIDS from 1982.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he was a Peace Corps volunteer in Ivory Coast (1964-66), a White House Fellow (1968-69) and a McKinsey associate; he also endowed Berkeley's Haas Scholars Program funding undergraduate research.
notes: Last on Forbes list in 1996; only listed source of wealth is Levi Strauss family stake. Haas Jr. Fund media contact is its Director of Communications (phone published on contact page). Age ~84; low public profile in recent years.

name: Huh Young-In
current_role: Chairman, SPC Group (Paris Baguette, Paris Croissant, BR Korea / Baskin-Robbins & Dunkin' Korea), Seoul
profile: Hur Young-in (b. 1949), second son of Samlip Food founder Hur Chang-sung, opened the Paris Croissant bakery in Seoul in 1986 and began franchising Paris Baguette in 1988, building SPC into Korea's largest bakery-food group with stores across Asia, the US and France. Sons Hur Jin-soo (vice chairman, Nov 2025) and Hur Hee-soo now run day-to-day; SPC is building a Texas bakery plant due 2027.
interesting_fact: France decorated him in 2010 and 2012 for helping make bread a staple of the South Korean diet; Paris Baguette now even operates bakeries in Paris.
deep_cut_fact: In 1981, already working in the family bakery business, he moved to the United States to formally study pastry and baking before launching Paris Croissant in 1986.
notes: Romanized variously as Hur/Huh/Heo Young-in. Has faced labour-related prosecution in 2024 (released on bail) and SPC had high-profile factory safety incidents - sensitive topics. No published press email found; route via SPC Group corporate communications.

name: Sachin Bansal
current_role: Executive Chairman, Navi Group (Navi Technologies / Navi Finserv), Bengaluru
profile: IIT Delhi graduate and ex-Amazon engineer who co-founded Flipkart with Binny Bansal in 2007 as an online bookstore; he exited when Walmart bought control in 2018. He then founded Navi (lending, insurance, mutual funds, UPI), putting much of his proceeds into it. In Feb 2025 he handed the CEO roles to Rajiv Naresh and Abhishek Dwivedi and became executive chairman.
interesting_fact: In 2026 he has said Navi is using AI to build its credit and fraud models, part of his pitch to make Navi a low-cost, tech-first financial services group.
deep_cut_fact: Flipkart's very first order (Oct 2007) was a copy of John Wood's 'Leaving Microsoft to Change the World' for VVK Chandra, a Hyderabad software engineer who found it via a link Bansal posted on his tech blog; the founders scoured Bangalore bookshops to find a copy.
notes: Input lists name as 'Sachin Bansaal' (Hurun India 2015 spelling) - this is Flipkart co-founder Sachin Bansal. navi.com blocked automated fetches so no press contact verified; reachable via Navi corporate communications and his public X presence (handle not verified here). Binny Bansal is unrelated despite the surname.

name: Chen Huwen
current_role: Chairman and co-founder, Shanghai M&G Stationery Inc. (晨光文具, SSE: 603899)
profile: Chen Huwen co-founded M&G Stationery, China's largest stationery brand, which grew from contract manufacturing into its own pens and school-supplies brand, a nationwide network of tens of thousands of retail stores, the Jiumu/9 Square lifestyle chain and the Colipu (科力普) office-supplies B2B arm. He holds an EMBA and has worked in stationery manufacturing since 1997.
interesting_fact: M&G began by making stationery under contract for Korean brands; when the 1997 Asian financial crisis took those clients down, the founders switched to their own brand, originally 'Sino-Korean M&G Stationery' (中韩晨光文具).
notes: Runs M&G alongside family co-founders (founder Chen Huxiong per Chinese Wikipedia). Very low media profile. IR contact (board secretary email/phone) is published in M&G's SSE annual reports on sse.com.cn/cninfo - not extracted here. Web search budget ran out during this person, so research is thinner.

name: Shashank Kumar
profile: IIT Roorkee B.Tech graduate who co-founded Razorpay with Harshil Mathur in 2014; it now runs India's largest payment gateway by transactions, serving 113 of India's top 125 unicorns, plus banking (RazorpayX), payroll and POS products. Privately held, it was last valued at about $7.5bn after raising $700m+ from investors including GIC and Mastercard.
interesting_fact: Razorpay has grown partly through acquisitions - eight to date, including a payroll-management business and a point-of-sale platform.
notes: Razorpay newsroom contact page also lists named corporate-communications staff. Fintech/infra founder - plausible podcast fit on payments/data infrastructure. Web search budget was exhausted before a sourced deep-cut fact could be found.

name: Andrea Della Valle
current_role: Vice Chairman, Tod's S.p.A. (Tod's, Hogan, Roger Vivier, Fay)
profile: Born 1965 in Sant'Elpidio a Mare in the Marche shoe district, Andrea and brother Diego control Tod's, the luxury shoe and leather-goods group grown from their grandfather's early-1900s workshop. In 2024 they took Tod's private with L Catterton and LVMH at a ~$1.5bn valuation. The brothers also hold stakes in Piaggio and RCS MediaGroup; Andrea chaired ACF Fiorentina 2004-09.
interesting_fact: Tod's group funded the restoration of Rome's Colosseum; Andrea also led Fiorentina's revival after its previous owner's bankruptcy and remained honorary president until the club was sold to Rocco Commisso in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: On 31 May 2024 the Marche mountain town of Arquata del Tronto, devastated by the 2016 earthquake, made him an honorary citizen 'for the social and civil commitment shown after the 2016 earthquake'.
notes: Brother Diego Della Valle is the public face of Tod's; Andrea is lower-profile. todsgroup.com blocked automated access, so press contact not extracted - check its Media/Contacts section manually. Web search budget exhausted at this point.
